subject: general
question: A rainbow is formed by water droplets suspended in the atmosphere after the rain shower. The phenomenon responsible for occurring of rainbow consists of:

options.text: A combination of refraction, dispersion and total internal reflection
A combination of refraction, scattering and dispersion

solution:
The correct answer is __**A combination of refraction, dispersion, and total internal reflection**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Refraction occurs when light enters a water droplet and slows down, causing the light to change direction.
 
• Dispersion happens as different colors of light bend by different amounts due to varying wavelengths.
 
• Total internal reflection occurs when light bounces off the inside surface of the droplet.
 
• The combination of these phenomena results in the spectrum of colors forming a circular arc, known as a rainbow.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Refraction:**

 
 
• Refraction is the bending of light as it passes from one medium to another with a different density.
 
• It is governed by Snell's Law, which relates the angles of incidence and refraction to the indices of refraction of the two media.
 
• This bending occurs because light travels at different speeds in different media.
 
 
 
• **Dispersion:**
 
 
• Dispersion is the process in which white light separates into its constituent colors (spectrum) when passing through a medium like a prism or water droplet.
 
• This occurs because different colors (wavelengths) of light bend by different amounts when they encounter a boundary between two media.
 
• In the case of a rainbow, dispersion causes the different colors to spread out and form the spectrum seen in the sky.
 
 
 
• **Total Internal Reflection:**
 
 
• Total internal reflection occurs when light hits the boundary of a medium at an angle larger than the critical angle, causing it to reflect entirely within the medium rather than passing through.
 
• This phenomenon is crucial in the formation of a rainbow as it ensures that light is reflected inside the water droplet and exits at the correct angle to be observed as a rainbow.
